dwelling_habits.dwelling: Roosts on mangroves and cliffs; soars over coastal water all day.
dwelling_habits.food: Fish snatched from the surface — and snacks stolen from other birds.
dwelling_habits.feeding: Pirate of the sky: harasses boobies until they drop a catch.
dwelling_habits.mating: Males inflate a huge red throat balloon to impress.
dwelling_habits.socializing: Colonies argue loudly; in air they look like flying Ws.

fun_facts: They can soar for hours without flapping — ocean hang-gliders.
Feathers aren’t very waterproof, so they rarely land on the sea.

dwelling_habits.dwelling: Open tropical oceans — floatsam lines, weed patches, and buoy shadows. Rarely a beach tourist; you’ll meet them farther offshore or on a plate.
dwelling_habits.food: Fast hunters of flying fish, squid, and whatever smaller fish hide under floating debris.
dwelling_habits.feeding: Accelerates like a sports car — chase, slash, gulp. Flashy gold-green colors intensify when they hunt or fight.
dwelling_habits.mating: Grows up shockingly fast and breeds often; big males (bulls) sport a high blunt forehead that kids compare to a swimming doorstop.
dwelling_habits.socializing: Often travel in pairs or small groups under the same bit of debris — roommates with fins.

fun_facts: “Mahi mahi” means “strong-strong” in Hawaiian — and they live up to the double name with double attitude.
They change colors like mood rings when excited… which is most of the time they’re around anglers.

dwelling_habits.dwelling: Aruba and ABC lagoons — often mixed with turtle grass in clear shallows.
dwelling_habits.feeding: Makes energy from sunlight (and sometimes from clear shallow water light).
dwelling_habits.mating: Spreads by spores, seeds, propagules, or creeping rhizomes depending on the species.
dwelling_habits.socializing: Forms habitat structure that shelters fish, crabs, and invertebrates.

fun_facts: Leaves look like green spaghetti waving in the current.
Part of Aruba’s native seagrass mix with turtle grass and shoal grass.
